new.title: The accountant who submits a bill can sign its first review stage themselves
new.body: Step 21 stops the person who submitted a fee from approving it. Step 23 does not do the same for the bill built from those fees. The bill resource has separationOfDuties set to false, so decide.ts never checks whether the reviewer is the submitter, and the queue filter does not hide the reviewer's own submissions. The seeded Bill review flow puts the accounting role on stage 1 ('all must pass'). The accounting role holds the whole expense subtree, so the same accountant has expense.bill.update to submit and expense.bill.review to decide. In an org with one accountant, that person groups the fees, submits the bill and passes stage 1 alone, which defeats the 'two sets of eyes on the figures' the flow promises. The bill then goes to invoicing and write-off with only the director's stage 2 behind it. The project's own concurrency test says it outright: an owner may review a bill they submitted.

new.title: Copy to payable fills every vendor cost with our selling price
new.body: At step 20 the SOP tells the operator to press Copy to payable to mirror the receivable rows into Payable details, and then only to type the vendor into Settlement unit. copyAcross spreads the whole receivable row (...r) into each new payable row, so quantity, unit price, amount and tax rate all come across as the customer's selling figures. The code deliberately blanks the settlement unit and the exchange rate, but not the price. Unless the operator retypes every unit price, each payable is recorded at what we charge the customer rather than what the vendor charges us. The SINGLE BILL TOTAL gross profit then shows about 0, and the payable bills built from these lines at step 22 carry the wrong amounts. Nothing flags a payable whose price equals its receivable twin.

new.title: Every new fee row starts in USD, whatever currency the branch works in
new.body: When the operator presses Costs name on the Expense entry page (step 20), the new row's currency is hard-coded to USD. When sales press Add Line on a quotation (step 6), the empty line also defaults to USD. The code comment admits this is 'OURS, NOT OBSERVED'. A Malaysian operator who types a ringgit amount and does not notice the currency cell saves a USD line. It is then converted at the USD rate, roughly four times too high, and flows into bills, invoices and Financial Stat looking complete. This is separate from the base-currency item: the branch currency exists (team.currency) but is not used as the default.

new.title: Before 8 am the payment date and decision date default to yesterday
new.body: The Add Payment dialog (step 26) pre-fills Pay and Receive Date, and the Decide dialog (step 10) pre-fills Decision date, with new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10). That is the UTC calendar date. In Malaysia (UTC+8), anything recorded between 00:00 and 07:59 local time silently gets the previous day. A receipt keyed by the cashier early on the 1st of the month is dated the last day of the prior month, so it lands in the wrong month in Financial Stat and the month-end pack. A Won/Lost entered early in the morning gets the wrong decision date. The field looks correctly filled, so it is rarely checked.
